basic.title: Basic Concepts
basic.intro: Understanding spoke dimensions, materials, and typical use cases is crucial for building a reliable wheelset that matches your riding style.

dtSwiss.name: DT Swiss (Switzerland)
dtSwiss.body: Renowned for stable craftsmanship and a comprehensive product matrix (straight, butted, aero), with complete engineering support.

sapim.name: Sapim (Belgium)
sapim.body: Leading in high-end aero spokes (e.g. CX-Ray). Known for lightweight performance and excellent fatigue life.

pillar.name: Pillar (Taiwan)
pillar.body: Strong cost-performance with a wide range including reinforced (PSR) designs. Suitable for custom and mass production.

mac.name: Mac / CNSpoke
mac.body: Fast supply chain response. Covers all types while balancing cost and performance for diverse applications.

yt.name: YT Spokes (China)
yt.body: Fast supply chain response, suitable for balancing cost and performance.

carbon.name: CARBON SPOKE
carbon.body: The pinnacle of lightweight performance. Designed for ultimate responsiveness and rigidity, drastically reducing rotational weight.

straight.title: Straight Gauge Spokes
straight.features: High strength margin, low cost, easy maintenance.
straight.use: Commuting, touring, cargo, high-tension drive sides.

butted.title: Double/Triple Butted
butted.features: Lighter, with better fatigue resistance from flex in the midsection.
butted.use: Endurance road, XC/Gravel, versatile durable builds.

aero.title: Bladed / Aero
aero.features: Aerodynamic, with easier torque control and anti-twist behavior.
aero.examples: Sapim CX-Ray, DT Aerolite, Pillar PSR X-TRA.
aero.use: Racing road, disc brake high-tension, aero rims.

straightPull.title: Straight-pull
straightPull.body: No elbow stress, fast building, specific hubs.

basic.disclaimer: The following comparison reflects relative performance characteristics across different spoke materials. Each material has its own strengths depending on the application. The listed pros and cons are not absolute judgments or defect classifications.

stainless.title: Stainless Steel
stainless.body: Currently the most mainstream and widely used spoke material on the market, offering the best balance of durability and cost.
stainless.marketBody: As detailed in the Basic Concepts above, the stainless steel spoke market is defined by the Big 2 (DT Swiss, Sapim) setting the quality benchmark, with Pillar and others offering competitive high-value alternatives. These major brands primarily utilize high-grade stainless steel (e.g. 18/8 or proprietary blends) for their main product lines.
stainless.bestFor: Almost all bicycles, from commuters to pro MTB/Road bikes.

carbon.title: Carbon Fiber
carbon.body: Found on high-end performance wheelsets. Offers extreme weight savings and rigidity.
carbon.bestFor: High-end road racing, time trials, and weight-focused builds.

titanium.title: Titanium Alloy
titanium.body: Middle ground between steel and carbon. High strength-to-weight ratio and no rust.
titanium.bestFor: Custom builds and riders valuing comfort and aesthetics.

aluminum.title: Aluminum Alloy
aluminum.body: Used by specific manufacturers (e.g. Campagnolo). Very light but can be problematic.

basic.conclusion: Which material you choose ultimately depends on your budget, riding style, and specific performance needs such as weight, stiffness, and comfort.

choose.title: Spoke Selection Matrix
choose.intro: Compare our supported spoke models to find the perfect match for your building goals, whether it is maximum durability, lightweight performance, or aerodynamic efficiency.

rows.name: SAPIM Leader
rows.details: Stainless (18/8). Strength: 1080-1180 N/mm². Durable straight gauge choice.

rows.name: SAPIM Race
rows.details: Strength: 1300 N/mm². Evolution of classic Competition. Good fatigue adaptability.

rows.name: SAPIM D-Light
rows.details: Strength: 1370 N/mm². Designed for top quality MTB/Disc wheels. Max strength, min weight.

rows.name: SAPIM CX-Sprint
rows.details: Strength: 1430 N/mm². Aero bladed. High stiffness for drive-side applications.

rows.name: SAPIM CX-Ray
rows.details: Strength: 1600 N/mm². The gold standard. Light as titanium, strong as steel. Highest fatigue life.

rows.name: SAPIM Super-CX
rows.details: Strength: 1430 N/mm². Lightest stainless spoke ever. Extra light wheels.

rows.name: Carbon Spoke
rows.details: Proprietary carbon manufacturing process. Provides 3x the specific stiffness of steel.

choose.weightBody: Weights listed are approximations for typical 64-piece (2 wheels, 32H) lengths (260mm-270mm).
